newsitem.title: UK: UK cabinet meets, no sign polling day discussed.
newsitem.headline: UK cabinet meets, no sign polling day discussed.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major's cabinet held a 1-1/2 hour meeting on Thursday, but ministers left his 10 Downing Street office without giving any indication that the timing of a general election had come under discussion.

An aide to Major said topics discussed at the meeting included the killing of a British soldier in Northern Ireland, recent economic statistics, the situation in the former Yugoslavia and the Great Lakes region of Africa and a forthcoming United Nations meeting on the environment.
"Whether there was a short (domestic) political section of the cabinet, I don't know," he added.

Political observers believe that if Major opts for an early general election on March 20, he will have to announce the date this week, possibly at Friday's annual conference of the Welsh Conservatives.
However, Major has indicated he may prefer to wait until May 1, before asking the electorate to give his party an unprecedented fifth consecutive term in office.
